translationRepairs: His paternal grandmother, Lady Qin, was posthumously titled Empress Yuan of Xiao'an.
His ancestress Lady Qin was posthumously titled Empress Yuan of Xiao'an.
祖妣秦氏 follows 四代祖璟 and his posthumous Xiao'an honors; she is that ancestor's consort, four generations above Gaozu, not his paternal grandmother.
His paternal grandmother, née Qin, was posthumously given the title Empress Yuan of Xiao'an.
His ancestress, née Qin, was posthumously given the title Empress Yuan of Xiao'an.
The literal field makes the same kinship error: 祖妣 here is Jingzu's consort, not Gaozu's paternal grandmother.
His third-generation ancestor Chen died young. He was posthumously made Left Regular Attendant of the Cavalry and honored as Emperor Xiaojian, with the temple name Suzu and the mausoleum Huiling.
His third-generation ancestor Chen died young. He was posthumously made Left Cavalier Attendant-in-ordinary and honored as Emperor Xiaojian, with the temple name Suzu and the mausoleum Huiling.
左散騎常侍 is the civil cavalier-attendant court office. 'Of the Cavalry' makes it sound like a cavalry command.
His paternal grandmother, Lady An, was posthumously titled Empress Gong of Xiaojian.
His ancestress Lady An was posthumously titled Empress Gong of Xiaojian.
祖妣安氏 follows 三代祖郴; she is Suzu's consort, not Gaozu's paternal grandmother.
His paternal grandmother, née An, was posthumously given the title Empress Gong of Xiaojian.
His ancestress, née An, was posthumously given the title Empress Gong of Xiaojian.
The literal field likewise names Lady An as paternal grandmother, but 祖妣 here is Chen's consort.

In the twelfth year of Tianyou, Zhuangzong brought all of Hebei under his control and opened his headquarters at Ye. Liang sent its senior general Liu Yan with fifty thousand troops to encamp at Shen.

In the twelfth year of Tianyou, Zhuangzong brought all of Hebei under his control and opened his headquarters at Ye. Liang sent its senior general Liu Xun with fifty thousand troops to encamp at Shen.
劉鄩 is Liu Xun (鄩 xún). Yan is a misreading of the given name.
In the twelfth year of Tianyou, Zhuangzong united the Hebei region, established his headquarters at Ye, and Liang sent its senior general Liu Yan with fifty thousand troops to encamp at Shen.
In the twelfth year of Tianyou, Zhuangzong united the Hebei region, established his headquarters at Ye, and Liang sent its senior general Liu Xun with fifty thousand troops to encamp at Shen.
The literal field repeats Liu Yan for 劉鄩; the name is Liu Xun.
In the second month of the thirteenth year, Yan marched his army in a sudden rush to Qingping and pressed up under the city walls.
In the second month of the thirteenth year, Xun marched his army in a sudden rush to Qingping and pressed up under the city walls.
Short 鄩 continues the same person; English Yan is the wrong reading.
In the second month of the thirteenth year, Yan led his troops in a sudden advance to Qingping and pressed close beneath the city walls.
In the second month of the thirteenth year, Xun led his troops in a sudden advance to Qingping and pressed close beneath the city walls.
The literal short name Yan likewise misreads 鄩 as Xun's given name.
Zhuangzong arrived from Ganling before the army had finished forming its ranks, and many units were caught and overrun by Yan.

多為鄩所掩 refers to Xun, not Yan.

The following year, Yan's army drew up northwest of Shen, and Mingzong fought alongside Zhuangzong in a hard-fought battle.
The following year, Xun's army drew up northwest of Shen, and Mingzong fought alongside Zhuangzong in a hard-fought battle.
鄩兵 is Xun's army, not Yan's.
The next year, Yan's army formed battle lines northwest of Shen, and Mingzong followed Zhuangzong in fierce fighting.
The next year, Xun's army formed battle lines northwest of Shen, and Mingzong followed Zhuangzong in fierce fighting.
The literal 鄩兵 likewise belongs to Xun.

After a long while dust blotted out the field on every side. Both the Emperor and Mingzong were caught inside the enemy formation. The Emperor threw himself forward with sword drawn and fought back and forth for miles, finally driving Yan east of the old Yuancheng.

逐鄩 is driving Xun, not Yan.

After a long while dust rose on all sides; the Emperor and Mingzong both fell into the midst of the enemy lines. The Emperor threw himself forward, sword drawn, and fought back and forth repeatedly, travelling several tens of li and driving Yan east of the old Yuancheng.

In the tenth month of the twentieth year, while following Mingzong to observe the Liang at Yangjia village, the troops were all without armor when the enemy suddenly came out and enveloped Mingzong. Blades were about to reach his back when the Emperor advanced with a battle halberd in hand. With one strike he knocked several enemy chieftains from their horses, and Mingzong was saved from danger.

In the tenth month of the twentieth year, while following Mingzong to observe the Liang at Yangcun stockade, the troops were all without armor when the enemy suddenly came out and enveloped Mingzong. Blades were about to reach his back when the Emperor advanced with a battle halberd in hand. With one strike he knocked several enemy chieftains from their horses, and Mingzong was saved from danger.
楊村寨 is Yangcun stockade; Yangjia misreads 村 as the surname Jia.

In the tenth month of the twentieth year, following Mingzong to observe the Liang at Yangjia village, the troops were all without armor when suddenly the enemy came out unexpectedly and used troops to envelop Mingzong; blades were about to reach his back when the Emperor advanced gripping a battle halberd, and with one strike several fierce chieftains fell from their horses; Mingzong was thus delivered from peril.

In the tenth month of the twentieth year, following Mingzong to observe the Liang at Yangcun stockade, the troops were all without armor when suddenly the enemy came out unexpectedly and used troops to envelop Mingzong; blades were about to reach his back when the Emperor advanced gripping a battle halberd, and with one strike several fierce chieftains fell from their horses; Mingzong was thus delivered from peril.
The literal field makes the same misreading of 楊村寨 as Yangjia village.
That year Zhuangzong took the throne at Ye, changed the era name to Tongguang, and sent Mingzong across the river with a detached force to advance deep and take Yan.
That year Zhuangzong took the throne at Ye, changed the era name to Tongguang, and sent Mingzong across the river with a detached force to advance deep and take Yun.
取鄆 is Yun, not Yan (燕).

That year Zhuangzong took the throne at Ye, changed the era name to Tongguang, and sent Mingzong across the river with an isolated army advancing deep to take Yun.

The people of Yan at first did not notice them. The Emperor followed Mingzong across the ford with fifty horsemen and burst in through the east gate.
The people of Yun at first did not notice them. The Emperor followed Mingzong across the ford with fifty horsemen and burst in through the east gate.
鄆人 are the people of Yun.

The people of Yun at first did not perceive them; the Emperor with fifty horsemen followed Mingzong across the ford, burst in through the east gate, and entered.
The literal 鄆人 are likewise people of Yun, not Yan.
Yan troops came to resist. The Emperor was struck by a blade, shielded Mingzong on both sides, arrayed his men across the main thoroughfare, and stood firm without moving.
Yun troops came to resist. The Emperor was struck by a blade, shielded Mingzong on both sides, arrayed his men across the main thoroughfare, and stood firm without moving.
鄆兵 are Yun troops, not Yan troops.

The literal 鄆兵 are likewise Yun troops.

At that time Yedu was the wealthiest place under heaven, but local customs were fierce and truculent and the people were much given to lawsuits. The Emperor ordered that complaint letters be deposited in a box at the government gate and read each one himself. After more than a year his desks were piled high, and many cases backloged in the courts; contemporary opinion lowered its estimate of him on this account.

The Emperor ordered that complaint letters be deposited in a box at the government gate, and he read each one in turn. After more than a year the desks were piled full, and many cases backloged in the courts; contemporary opinion lowered its estimate of him on this account.

In the ninth month Dong Zhang of Dongchuan rebelled; the court appointed the Emperor eastern campaign marshal and commander-in-chief of the Dongchuan expeditionary forces, with concurrent control of the Dongchuan expeditionary headquarters.

In the ninth month Dong Zhang of Dongchuan rebelled; the court appointed the Emperor commander-in-chief of the Dongchuan expeditionary forces, with concurrent control of the Dongchuan expeditionary headquarters.
The Chinese names only 東川行營都招討使 and concurrent 知東川行府事. 'Eastern campaign marshal' is an invented extra office.
In every command where he served he made filial governance a priority. When he saw parents and sons dividing property against brothers, he always had them bound and executed.
In every command where he served he made filial governance a priority. When he saw brothers dividing and seizing property while their parents were still living, he always had them bound and executed.
父母在昆弟分索 marks brothers who divided family property while their parents were still living, not parents and sons dividing against brothers.

In the fifth month of the third year he was transferred to military commissioner of Yanzhou, advanced in enfeoffment to Duke of Zhao, and given the title Meritorious Minister Who Supports Heaven, Initiates Fortune, and Upholds Rectitude.

In the fifth month of the third year he was transferred to military commissioner of Yunzhou, advanced in enfeoffment to Duke of Zhao, and his title was changed to Meritorious Minister Who Supports Heaven, Initiates Fortune, and Upholds Rectitude.
鄆州 is Yunzhou, not Yanzhou (兗州), and 仍改 means the meritorious-minister title was changed, not merely given.

The Emperor and the Khitan had originally no pact of friendship; after the Last Emperor pressed him, he sent his trusted man He Fu with a knife and file as tokens of faith; with one word the other came personally to his distress, swift as flowing lightning—is this the trust of Heaven's intent!

The Emperor and the Khitan had originally no pact of friendship; after the Last Emperor pressed him, he sent his trusted man He Fu with a knife and file as tokens of faith; with one word the other came personally to his distress, swift as flowing lightning—was this truly Heaven's intent!
The first 信 is the knife-and-file token; 信天意耶 uses 信 as 'truly' and asks whether the rescue was Heaven's intent, not 'the trust of Heaven's intent.'

I have lately seen that the solitary man Congke, not of the public clan, stole the precious design, abandoned righteousness and forgot kindness, defied Heaven and ravaged creatures, executed and cut down his own kin, set loyal men at odds, listened to flattery and deceit, tyrannized the black-haired people, made Chinese and barbarians tremble in fear, and caused inner and outer collapse; knowing you were innocent, he brought harm upon you for it.

I have lately seen that the solitary man Congke, not of the imperial clan, stole the precious design, abandoned righteousness and forgot kindness, defied Heaven and ravaged creatures, executed and cut down his own kin, set loyal men at odds, listened to flattery and deceit, tyrannized the black-haired people, made Chinese and barbarians tremble in fear, and caused inner and outer collapse; knowing you were innocent, he brought harm upon you for it.
本非公族 means Congke was not of the imperial/ruling clan. 'Public clan' is a mistranslation of 公族.

Moreover, the Last Emperor was a man of Zhending and Changshan; he had an ancestral old residence, and beside it an ancient Buddhist monastery with a stone image that suddenly shook without cease, and all regarded it as strange.

Moreover, the Last Emperor was a man of Zhending in Changshan; he had an ancestral old residence, and beside it an ancient Buddhist monastery with a stone image that suddenly shook without cease, and all regarded it as strange.
真定常山人 names Zhending in Changshan commandery, not two coordinate native places joined by and.

(The 《Khitan State Annals》 cites the 《Record of Strange Events》: The Khitan ruler Deguang often napped by day and dreamed of a divine man with a flowered crown and beautiful countenance, with very abundant plum blossoms in his carriage, who suddenly descended from Heaven, wore white robes, bore a golden belt, and grasped an axe. Twelve strange men followed behind him, and among them a black rabbit entered Deguang's bosom and vanished.

(The 《Khitan State Annals》 cites the 《Record of Strange Events》: The Khitan ruler Deguang often napped by day and dreamed of a divine man with a flowered crown and beautiful countenance, with a very splendid covered carriage, who suddenly descended from Heaven, wore white robes, bore a golden belt, and grasped a mace. Twelve strange men followed behind him, and among them a black rabbit entered Deguang's bosom and vanished.
Qidan Guozhi reads 輜軿甚盛, a covered-carriage binome; the chapter's 輜梅 is that reading, not plum blossoms. Chapter 钅骨钅朵 is 骨朵, a mace, not an axe.
